name: battery.charging.get
doc: {} → {available, supported, enabled, start, end, devices}: GNOME's Battery Charging (Energie en batterij › Batterij opladen): the batteries that power the computer (UPower EnumerateDevices, Type 2, PowerSupply), supported when one has ChargeThresholdSupported, enabled when every supported one has ChargeThresholdEnabled (Batterijgezondheid behouden), start and end its ChargeStart/EndThreshold; event battery.changed with the same state when a threshold property changes

name: battery.charging.set
doc: {enabled} → battery.charging.get's answer: UPower Device EnableChargeThreshold(enabled) on every battery that supports it, with interactive authorization (polkit org.freedesktop.UPower.enable-charging-limit; Maximale lading = false, Batterijgezondheid behouden = true); error unsupported battery.unavailable / battery.noChargeLimit; a dry run sends nothing

name: battery.history
doc: {type?:'charge'|'rate' (charge), timespan?:seconds 60-2592000 (86400), resolution?:points 2-2000 (200)} → {available, type, timespan, device, points:[[time, value, state]]}: UPower Device GetHistory of the first battery with HasHistory, oldest first (Energie en batterij › Batterijniveaus: Afgelopen 24 uur / Afgelopen 7 dagen); state is UPower's (1 charging, 2 discharging, 4 fully charged)

name: display.apply
doc: {serial, method:'verify'|'temporary'|'persistent', logical:[{x, y, scale, transform, primary, monitors:[{connector, mode, props?:{underscanning?, color-mode?, rgb-range?}}]}], props?:{layout-mode?}} → {ok, method, confirm:'settings'|'shell'|'none', id?, timeout?}: Mutter's ApplyMonitorsConfig (notes/claude/settings-parity.md 5.5); a persistent change is verified first, then extension/displayBridge.js holds back GNOME Shell's own keep dialog and relays display.confirmChange {timeout, id} (confirm 'settings', answer with display.confirm) or GNOME Shell asks itself (confirm 'shell'); mutter reverts after 20 s without an answer (amendments 32, 64, 69)

name: display.confirm
doc: {keep, id?} → {ok, kept, pending}: Settings' answer to the keep-changes question of a persistent display.apply (GNOME Shell's complete_display_change through displayBridge.js); pending false when no question was open

name: display.identify
doc: {} → {ok, labels:{connector: n}}: GNOME's monitor labels (Main.osdMonitorLabeler through displayBridge.js) for 3 s with display.state's numbers; error unsupported without the bridge

name: display.nightLight.disableUntilTomorrow
doc: {on} → the night-light status: gsd-color's DisabledUntilTomorrow (Nachtlampje's Nu uitschakelen / Nu inschakelen, amendment 25); the schedule is never rewritten; event display.nightLight.changed

name: display.nightLight.status
doc: {} → {available, supported, active, disabledUntilTomorrow, temperature, sunrise, sunset}: gsd-color's night light (session bus org.gnome.SettingsDaemon.Color) and mutter's NightLightSupported; event display.nightLight.changed

name: display.state
doc: {} → {supported, backend:'mutter'|'hyprland'|'none', serial, allowed, nightLightSupported, panelOrientationManaged, layoutMode, supportsChangingLayoutMode, globalScaleRequired, monitors:[{connector, vendor, product, serial, displayName, builtin, forLease, underscanning, privacyScreen, minRefreshRate, colorMode, colorModes, rgbRange, modes:[{id, width, height, refresh, preferredScale, scales, current, preferred, interlaced, variable}], current, preferred, logical, x, y, scale, transform, primary}], logical:[{x, y, scale, transform, primary, monitors}]}: Mutter's GetCurrentState decoded; event display.changed {what:'monitors'|'properties'}

name: sound.alerts.get
doc: {} → {alert:'none'|'default'|'click'|'string'|'swing'|'hum', choices, available, eventSounds, theme, defaultTheme, writable, startupSound, startupAvailable, startupWritable}: GNOME Settings' alert sound (org.gnome.desktop.sound event-sounds, theme-name and the __custom theme's bell link) and Ubuntu's startup sound (org.gnome.shell.ubuntu startup-sound), for Meer geluidsinstellingen › Geluiden (amendment 3)

name: sound.alerts.set
doc: {alert?, theme?, eventSounds?, startupSound?} → sound.alerts.get's answer: none = event-sounds false; default = event-sounds true and theme-name back to its default; click/string/swing/hum = GNOME's __custom theme in $XDG_DATA_HOME/sounds (index.theme, bell-terminal.ogg and bell-window-system.ogg links) and theme-name '__custom'; startupSound = startup-sound 'warty-startup' or ''. Every key is checked before a file is written; a dry run writes nothing

name: sound.meter
doc: {kind:'sink'|'source', name, on} → {ok, on, lease}: a level meter (a peak-detect record stream on the source or the sink's monitor, as GNOME Settings' level bars, with its application.id so GNOME Shell's microphone indicator skips it); events sound.level {kind, name, peak 0..1} about 25 times a second; on: true starts or renews the 30 s lease, on: false stops it

name: sound.moveStream
doc: {kind:'sinkInput'|'sourceOutput', index, device} → {ok}: an app's playback or recording to another sink or source (Volumemixer's per-app Uitvoerapparaat / Invoerapparaat; pa_context_move_sink_input_by_index)

name: sound.setBalance
doc: {sink, balance?:-1..1, fade?:-1..1, lfe?:percent, volume?:percent, left?, right?} → {ok}: GNOME's balance, fade and subwoofer sliders (pa_cvolume_set_balance / _set_fade / _set_position on the sink's channel map; volume scales first); left and right (percent, both, instead of volume and balance) are Windows' Linkerkanaal and Rechterkanaal as one write

name: sound.setDefault
doc: {kind:'sink'|'source', name?, port?, card?, profile?} → {ok, device}: the default output or input (pa_context_set_default_sink/_source), with the port; when card and profile name a port whose profile is not active (sound.state's outputs/inputs), the profile is switched first and the new device waited for (GNOME's gvc_mixer_control_change_output)

name: sound.setEventVolume
doc: {volume:0..100, mute?} → {ok}: Systeemgeluiden, module-stream-restore's sink-input-by-media-role:event (GNOME's System Sounds; pa_ext_stream_restore_write)

name: sound.setMute
doc: {kind:'sink'|'source'|'sinkInput'|'sourceOutput', name? | index?, mute} → {ok}: mute a device or an app's stream

name: sound.setPort
doc: {kind:'sink'|'source', name, port} → {ok}: a device's port (Luidsprekers, Koptelefoon, ...; pa_context_set_sink_port_by_index)

name: sound.setProfile
doc: {card, profile} → {ok}: a card's profile (Indeling; 'off' = Audio: Niet toestaan, the profile before is remembered as the card's restore in sound.state)

name: sound.setVolume
doc: {kind:'sink'|'source'|'sinkInput'|'sourceOutput', name? | index?, volume:percent} → {ok}: the loudest channel to volume, the balance kept (pa_cvolume_scale, as GNOME); above 100 % only up to GNOME's maximum (about 153 %) while allow-volume-above-100-percent is on; a volume above 0 unmutes

name: sound.state
doc: {} → {available, server, version, defaultSink, defaultSource, maxVolume, outputs:[{id, kind, title, subtitle, device, port, card, profile, default, available, icon, formFactor, bus}], inputs, sinks:[{index, name, description, card, ports, activePort, volume, channels, balance, fade, lfe, canBalance, canFade, hasLfe, mute, default, monitor, state, icon, objectId}], sources (monitorOf), cards:[{index, name, description, profiles, activeProfile, off, restore, ports, outputs, inputs}], streams:[{index, kind:'output'|'input', app, icon, appId, name, role, volume, mute, device, volumeWritable}], eventVolume, eventMute}: the PulseAudio server (pipewire-pulse) through libpulse on the Sound service's own GLib context (amendment 39); outputs/inputs are GNOME Settings' device lists; event sound.changed with the same state; {available:false} without a server

name: sound.test
doc: {sink?, channel?, alert?} → {ok, played}: GNOME's speaker test (libcanberra audio-channel-<channel> forced onto that channel of the sink) or an alert of the Geluidsschema (none, default, click, string, swing, hum); error unsupported without libcanberra

name: storage.cleanTemp
doc: {sense?:bool} → {ok, via:'gsd'|'host', removed?, freed?, failed?} | {ok, age, temp, trash, freed}: without sense GNOME's Delete Temporary Files (gsd-housekeeping RemoveTempFiles on the session bus; without it the host deletes this user's files in g_get_tmp_dir() itself, as gsd does); sense:true is Opslaginzicht nu uitvoeren, gsd-housekeeping's hourly purge with org.gnome.desktop.privacy now: temporary files older than old-files-age days when remove-old-temp-files, Prullenbak items deleted more than old-files-age days ago when remove-old-trash-files (temp/trash null when off; counts removed, freed bytes, failed); a dry run deletes nothing

name: wellbeing.history
doc: {} → {available, today, active, parental, days:[{date:'YYYY-MM-DD', weekday:1-7, seconds}]}: GNOME's Screen Time statistics from gnome-shell's $XDG_DATA_HOME/gnome-shell/session-active-history.json, summed per local day from the first record (at most 14 weeks) to today; available false for a malformed file, days empty without one; parental: malcontent limits this user's sessions (AccountsService com.endlessm.ParentalControls.SessionLimits LimitType)
